blockers.quote: Your own chip started from a crowd too. Last year, over 9 lakh people applied for UPSC's civil services exam. And 958 got in (c01). About one in a thousand.
blockers.why: Story #7 fails: three numbers arrive together, followed by another statistic before the first fact lands on you.
blockers.fix: Replace lines 86–91 with: “Last year, about one in a thousand UPSC applicants got in (c01). You wore that crowd's starting number like a verdict. But yours already moved down when you copied.” Cut c02 here.

blockers.quote: And yours? Here's the number nobody puts on a coaching poster. Of the people who reached last year's interview room... about one in three got in (c03).
blockers.why: Story #7 fails: this late fact causes no action or realization within two lines and interrupts the emotional payoff with another statistic.
blockers.fix: Cut lines 141–143 and move directly from “But it's his. And it's moving.” to the final row-three scene.

suggestions.fix: Specify a card entrance or slow camera drift so the three-second ident never becomes a still frame.

suggestions.fix: Keep the hold, but add a slow push toward the chip or a reflection sliding across the window.

keep.quote: You can't borrow someone's odds. Only their apron.
The biggest number? It tells you what's likely. It can't tell you what's worth choosing.
You know your number now. And you don't look up.
